name: Explorer
description: Find and explain existing code and repository behavior; choosing an approach belongs to Planner.
capacity: Reasoning must trace dependencies and explain evidence accurately. Responsive exploration helps; context should cover the relevant repository paths.

name: Researcher
description: Verify external facts and produce sourced findings, rather than map a local repository.
capacity: Reasoning must compare sources and resolve conflicting evidence. Accuracy matters more than speed; long context helps with documents and citations.

name: Planner
description: Choose an approach, make decisions and produce an actionable plan; implementation and worker management are separate work.
capacity: Strong reasoning must weigh constraints and tradeoffs. Speed is secondary to sound decisions; context should cover requirements and system boundaries.

name: Coder
description: Make and verify changes, including fault diagnosis, UI design, tests and documentation.
capacity: Strong coding and reasoning must support correct changes and verification. Speed helps in edit loops; long context helps with large repositories.

name: Reviewer
description: Independently assess changes or proposals, including security and second-opinion critique; implementing fixes is separate work.
capacity: Careful reasoning must find defects and assess evidence independently. Thoroughness matters more than speed; context should cover the change and affected callers.

name: Coordinator
description: Divide and delegate work, manage dependencies and combine results; each worker owns its implementation.
capacity: Reasoning must track dependencies and reconcile worker results. Responsive round trips help; context should retain the shared goal, assignments and evidence.

name: Generalist
description: Handle mixed end-to-end work when no specialist fits, rather than replace every narrower role.
capacity: Balanced reasoning must connect different kinds of work. Interactive speed helps; context should cover the full task and its changing requirements.

name: Utility
description: Produce bounded auxiliary outputs such as titles, commit messages, classifications and straightforward transformations. Small output does not imply low capability; faithful summarization and memory extraction are not automatically trivial utility work.
capacity: Reasoning must preserve meaning and satisfy the output contract. Speed helps repeated calls; context must fit the source material even when the output is short. Bounded work is not necessarily cheap or easy.
